reason: Under 'Add reboot actions to Amazon CloudWatch alarms' the quote states the reboot action is recommended for Instance Health Check failures and the recover action is suited for System Health Check failures.

The quote says that with available capital and a focus on maximum efficiency you benefit most from All Upfront when available, prepaying for compute at the highest discount; the condition is kept in the qualifiers.

The quote states account-level settings set directly or by declarative policy, configured in each Region, applied across Regions and accounts by a policy, and not modifiable in the account while a policy is in use.
The note states the feature only controls public AMIs or AMIs shared with your account and that AMIs created by your account are always discoverable and usable.

The table row 'Existing accounts with no public AMIs' carries footnote 1: an account that had a public AMI on or after July 15, 2023 is disabled by default even if all AMIs are now private; the claim drops this condition. The rest (blocking, existing public AMIs stay public) is supported.

The quotes state CopyImage keeps the source snapshots' encryption state without parameters, that a new encryption state can be applied by supplying parameters, and that with Encrypted set an unencrypted snapshot is encrypted by the account's default KMS key; the encryption-by-default condition is in the qualifiers.
The quote states AWS does not copy launch permissions or S3 bucket permissions and that you can apply them to the new AMI after the copy completes.
The quote states every part: software to set up and boot, a block device mapping, an AMI must be specified at launch, and it must be compatible with the instance type.
The quote and its list in context state an AMI with encrypted volumes or snapshots of encrypted volumes can't be made public but can be shared with specific AWS accounts.
The quotes state AMIs with encrypted snapshots can be shared across accounts and that volumes from unencrypted snapshots can be encrypted, some or all, at launch.
Under 'Launch permissions' the quotes and table state who can launch, public for all accounts, explicit for accounts, organizations or OUs, and that only the owner specifies launch permissions.
The AMIs row under 'Default quota per Region' gives 50,000 public and private AMIs including available, pending, disabled and Recycle Bin AMIs.
The quote states AMIs are Region-specific, must be in the Region of launch, and must be copied from the source Region to each target Region.
Under 'Root volume type' the quotes state EBS-backed root from an EBS snapshot for Linux and Windows, and S3-backed instance store root from an S3 template for Linux only.
Under 'Launch with no encryption parameters' the quotes state an owned encrypted snapshot keeps the same KMS key and a shared one is encrypted by your account's default KMS key.
The AMI sharing row gives a default of 1,000 entities per Region and says accounts inside a shared organization or OU do not count towards the quota.
The quotes state you can create an AMI from your instance, copy it to another Region, share it with other accounts, and launch multiple instances with the same configuration from one AMI.
The 'Boot time for an instance' row gives usually less than 1 minute for EBS-backed and usually less than 5 minutes for S3-backed AMIs.
The 'Modifications' row states instance type, kernel, RAM disk and user data can change while stopped for EBS-backed, and attributes are fixed for life for S3-backed.
The 'Stopped state' row states EBS-backed can be stopped with the root persisted in EBS, and S3-backed cannot be stopped and is running or terminated.
The quote states to call the EC2 API from your VPC using private IP addresses, use AWS PrivateLink.
In the list of what clients of the EC2 API must support, the quote states 'We require TLS 1.2 and recommend TLS 1.3.'
Under 'Background or batch processing' the quote states Spot gives significant savings for delayable work because occasional interruption is minimal business risk.
The quote and its sentence in context state the basic solution is manually attaching a network interface or Elastic IP to a replacement instance and the automated one is EC2 Auto Scaling.
Under the Security best practices the quote states to manage access using identity federation with an identity provider and IAM roles whenever possible.
The quote states Amazon Inspector automatically discovers and scans EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure.
The Security best practice quote states to implement the least permissive rules for your security group.
Under 'Backup and recovery' the quote states to deploy critical components across multiple Availability Zones and replicate data appropriately.
Under 'Resource management' the quote states to plan to request limit increases in advance of the time you need them.
Under 'Storage' the quote states to use separate EBS volumes for the OS and data and ensure the data volume persists after termination.
The claim repeats the quote: the T family gives a baseline CPU performance with the ability to burst above it at any time for as long as required.
Under the FAQ 'Burstable Instances' heading the quote states a CPU Credit provides the performance of a full CPU core for one minute.
Under 'Credit accrual limit' the quote states it depends on instance size and in general equals the maximum credits earned in 24 hours.
Under 'Accrued CPU credits life span' the quotes state credits on a running instance do not expire, T2 loses all credits on stop, and T8i, T4g, T3a and T3 keep the balance for seven days.
The quote states low-to-moderate CPU workloads waste CPU cycles so you pay for more than you use, and that low-cost burstable T instances overcome this.
The quotes state unlimited Spot Instances used immediately and briefly with no idle time incur surplus credit charges, and AWS recommends launching T4g or T3 Spot Instances in standard mode.
The quote states each burstable instance continuously earns credits below the CPU baseline and spends credits when it bursts above it.
The quotes state up to 15% savings compared to M instances, sizes as low as 2 vCPUs and 0.5 GiB, and the family T8i, T4g, T3a, T3 plus previous generation T2.
The quotes state launch credits are only applicable to T2 instances in Standard mode and that T8i, T4g, T3a and T3 do not earn launch credits.

The quotes state the hourly price covers all spikes when average CPU is at or below baseline over a rolling 24 hours or the lifetime, whichever is shorter, and prolonged higher use costs a flat additional rate per vCPU-hour.
